<!-- pr-reviewer: 976cda6c06735a09301393e61b652f899f908225 -->
BUILD: on the self-hosted runner, green: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43545643337 (merged with main f2b42e3d; quick gate: sim 111 s, motion 3 s, app 937 s, ui 40 s, 4 steps, 0 failed; clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings clean). No cfg(windows) or per-OS value in the diff, so no local run was owed.

**Needs changes before merge** - one gouge-passing case I cannot show is refused or bounded; everything else looks sound.

## What looks good
- Nothing is looser on the operation side: Engrave/Trace go None -> Mark, the whole-model pocket family None -> Keep (only with a stock set up, as before), picks stay Section, stock sources stay None apart from the new keep_parts check. Both laws sit in the only two frame arms of run_job_arms. `uncovered()` is not in the diff and does not read `DepthLaw`, so "unchanged" holds.
- `credit_marks` is bounded: it credits only columns the mark's own cutter swept, to `max(own sweep, part top - budget)`, never deepens a verdict, recomputes the budget from params + tool each run (not from the cached path), and another op cutting under the mark in the same column is still charged (pinned).
- `credit_floors` keeps every guard of the old `credit_breaks` walk; edge-break behaviour reads unchanged.
- `budget()` returns 0 for NaN, infinity, negative and Bottom-over-Top, and is capped by the radius.
- Refusal is a blocking `Warning::Gouge` on the move with a note naming the budget; pinned generate-then-post on both stocks and over MCP.
- No unwrap/expect/panic outside tests, tests live in the owning crates, no camcraft-* dependency added, decision file present, body complete.

## Requested before merge
1. **A plate thinner than the mark budget: a cut through the whole part reads as a mark, 0 findings, and the sim credits it too.** `mark_law::budget` (mark_law.rs, `min(Top - Bottom, cutter radius)`) is not bounded by the part's own thickness under the cutter. With a 2 mm plate, a 6 mm cutter and Top - Bottom >= 3, the part lowered by the budget lies wholly below the cutter, so `mark_into` finds nothing; `credit_marks` (sim mark.rs) uses floor `part top - budget`, which is below the plate's bottom, so the sim forgives the same column. A through-cut of the finished part would post clean. I could not show from the code or the tests that this is refused or bounded elsewhere, and no test pins it either way. Fix suggestion: cap the budget by the part's thickness in the column (law and credit alike), or refuse when the lowered part leaves nothing under the cutter; add a thin-plate pin on both stocks.
2. **Shank/holder checks run against the part lowered by the budget** (`mark_into` lowers every facet, then `solid_hits` reports ShankHit/RapidInStock). A shank or holder touching a wall top within the budget (up to the cutter radius) is excused. The op had no solid check before, so it is not a regression, but it is a looseness the decision file does not state. Please run the shank/holder checks against the unlowered part, or state and pin the excuse.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
- `budget_of` (sim) omits the `!material.facets.is_empty()` half of `part_solid_of`; only matters if the sim's part and the op's source differ. A one-line test would settle it.
- No test asserts the sim budget and the generate-time budget agree for a plane-frame (3+2) op; the PR body says 3+2 keep is not exercised.
- `generate.rs` (3530 lines) and `stock_sim.rs` (477) were already over 400 and grew; new logic is in new files.
- Follow-up #1607 (stock-source Engrave/Trace, P1) stays open as the author says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 976cda6c06735a09301393e61b652f899f908225 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** I found no blockers. There are four notes below that the maintainer should read. Two of them are pre-existing gaps that the probes turned up, and neither was introduced here.

### What looks good
- The mark law is judged on the real mesh, not on the typed Top. The part is lowered by `min(Top - Bottom, r)` and the solid law is run against it, so a Top typed under the surface, a wall beside the line, and a cut past the radius are all convicted (`mark_law.rs:427-459`). Lowering along Z is the safe direction on a slope: the depth it allows normal to the face is `b*cos(theta)`, which is never more than `b`.
- The sim credit is bounded in both directions: `floor = max(mark's own sweep, part top - budget)` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/mark.rs:829-836`). A column the mark never swept keeps the sharp verdict. Another operation's cut under a shallow mark is still charged. The budget is computed fresh from the op's parameters (`budget_of`) and is never read from the cache. A stock-source Engrave declares no mark.
- `credit_breaks` was refactored onto the shared `credit_floors` walk with its behaviour unchanged (`edge_break_credit` passes).
- The pocket family on a stock source now judges against the setup's parts, which closes the turned-stock case of #1554 on the op.
- There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests, the new modules carry provenance lines, both new suites have gate maps, there is a decision file, the PR body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes`, and there are no CHANGELOG, golden or snapshot changes.

### Results merged with `upstream/main` f2b42e3d (built locally)
The self-hosted runner was not usable (the runner list returned 403), so everything ran locally on macOS with sccache. The trial merge was clean ("already up to date": the branch already contains f2b42e3d).

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-sim lib + all sim test binaries (incl. `mark_credit` 6, `edge_break_credit` 5) | 595 passed, 0 failed |
| app `engrave_law` | 9 passed |
| app `keep_law` | 7 passed |
| app `whole_model_pocket` / `trochoid_law` / `circular_entity_law` / `circular_pick_law` | 5 / 6 / 4 / 4 passed |
| app `slot_picks` / `slot_pick_refusals` | 8 / 3 passed |
| app `lead_approach` / `machine_switch` / `post_not_judged` / `tilt` | 6 / 6 / 4 / 8 passed |
| app `setup_stock_source` / `stock_source_verdict` / `edge_break_gate` | 8 / 22 / 5 passed |
| app `solid_law` / `solid_law_goldens` / `golden_cl` | 4 / 7 / 32 passed |
| app `verify` / `mcp_verify` / `posting` / `operations` | 21 / 3 / 17 / 119 passed |
| app `area_controls` / `roughing2d` / `mill2d_b` / `mill2d_c` / `coarse_laws` / `stock_sim_document` | 13 / 7 / 9 / 9 / 6 / 9 passed |
| app lib | 246 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean. The `fixture_mesh_convict.rs:152` lint the body mentions does not fire on this merge. |

**Mutation checks (my own, each reverted):**
- In the sim credit I replaced the floor `z.max(p - budget)` with `p - budget`, so the full budget was credited wherever the mark swept. `a_budget_wider_than_the_cut_credits_only_what_the_cutter_swept` goes red, so the credit's scope is pinned. The author's M1-M12 table covers the budget formula, the lowering and the scope.

**Adversarial probes (a throwaway local test file, not pushed):**

| Probe | Aligned stock | Turned stock |
|---|---|---|
| `Milling-test.step` (STEP), whole-model Engrave and Trace, EM-0600, 0.3 mm deep | 0 findings, posts | 0 findings, posts |
| same, **3.0 mm (exactly the radius limit)** | 0 findings, posts | 0 findings, posts |
| same, 3.2 mm | op Gouge; sim charges 0.20 mm | op Gouge, refused by the op's moves |
| `Milling-test.step`, whole-model 2D Pocket, defaults, stock top to Z10 | 0 findings, posts | 0 findings, posts |
| `Milling-test.step`, whole-model **2D Adaptive**, defaults, stock top to Z10 | 3 op Gouges; **sim agrees: worst 10.00 mm at (-1.44, -29.94)** | 3 op Gouges, refused |
| Two parts side by side; Trace on B whose flank runs 2.3 mm into the taller part A | sim refuses (worst 2.00 mm) | **op records no Gouge for A** (the post was blocked only by an unrelated rapid in my fixture) |
| No stock set up, whole-model Pocket with Area offset +3 on a 30x30x10 block | (no sim) 0 findings, **posts** | - |

On the safety questions:
- **Can the credit excuse a real gouge?** I could not make it. Overlapping marks take the per-column minimum of each mark's `max(sweep, top - budget)`, and each of those is a legal floor for its own mark. A cut past the budget, an off-model wander back into a wall, and another op's cut under the mark all stay charged.
- **The three changed fixtures are real cuts into the part.** The stock-source pockets in `post_not_judged.rs` and `machine_switch.rs` cleared the whole stock while the part filled it. Shrinking the part to what the pocket leaves keeps the tests' intent. In `lead_approach.rs` the user's stock-source pocket runs from the model top to Z10 across the whole footprint, so it cuts the D-plate. The new filter (`beside_the_cut_part`, `lead_approach.rs:107-110`) asserts that gouge and then drops every `Gouge` warning. That loses no coverage against main, because on main a stock-source op had no part law, so a part gouge could never appear there.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **Whole-model 2D Adaptive with default controls cuts through `Milling-test.step`.** This is a pre-existing generator defect that this PR now catches. In the probe above, the op's law and the program sim independently agree on a 10 mm cut at (-1.44, -29.94), once per level (moves 146, 498, 850). Before this PR the turned-stock case would have posted. The body says "legal defaults post" for Adaptive, which holds on the #12 boss fixture but not on the user's part. I suggest filing a follow-up (refused visibly, so `P3` by the table) for the generator.
2. **Cross-part marks.** The mark and keep laws judge only the source entity's mesh. A Trace on part B whose flank enters a neighbouring part A has no op finding, so on a turned stock nothing judges A. The aligned sim does catch it, and the credit holds A to the budget. This gap predates the PR and applies equally to `Section`-law ops on B. It belongs next to #1607 and may deserve its own issue.
3. **A mark scales with the cutter.** `budget = min(Top - Bottom, r)` lets a whole-model Engrave with a 12.7 mm end mill post a 6.35 x 6.35 mm rabbet along every model edge. That fits the law as written and the issue's "depth budget" suggestion, but it is a channel more than a mark. The maintainer may want an absolute cap, or a cap tied to the tool type, recorded in `docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md`.
4. **No stock means no judge.** With no stock set up, `Keep` stands down (`generate.rs:2865-2870`) and a whole-model pocket with offset +3 posts with 0 findings. That is the documented #12 contract (the model is the volume to remove), so it is not a regression, but it is unjudged. It is worth confirming this is intended for a project that simply has not had its stock set yet.
5. `generate.rs` (3530 lines) grew by about 64 and `stock_sim.rs` (477 lines) by 10. Both were already over 400. The new logic sits in new files.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 976cda6c06735a09301393e61b652f899f908225 -->
**Correction: Needs changes before merge.** This replaces the "Ready" verdict in my review above, which crossed with NeoTech's review. I reproduced NeoTech's thin-plate case: it is a gouge that passes on both stocks, and I missed it in my probes.

### Reproduction (local, the PR merged with `upstream/main` f2b42e3d)
Part: a 40 x 40 x 2 mm plate (Z 0..2) in a 40 x 40 x 2 box stock. Tool: EM-0600-4FL (r 3). Source: the whole model. Top Z2, Bottom Z-0.9, so `budget = min(2.9, 3) = 2.9`.

| Kind | Stock | Deepest move | Blocking findings | Post |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Engrave | aligned | Z -0.900 | none | **posts** |
| Engrave | turned 90 deg | Z -0.900 | none | **posts** |
| Trace | aligned | Z -0.900 | none | **posts** |
| Trace | turned 90 deg | Z -0.900 | none | **posts** |

The cutter goes right through the finished plate along every edge it follows. Two things let it through:
- The op law (`mark_law.rs:427-459`) lowers the plate to Z -2.9..-0.9, so the cutter at Z -0.9 is only tangent to it.
- The sim credit (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/mark.rs:829-836`) uses the floor `max(sweep, top - budget) = -0.9` and forgives the column.

The same holds for a narrow rib or wall that is shorter than the budget: the mark can sever it. I had reasoned only about a wall that is narrow, not one that is short, and I withdraw my "the credit cannot excuse a real gouge" line.

### Requested before merge
1. **Bound the mark by the material under the cutter** (NeoTech's item 1, which I concur with). Change the op law and the sim credit together. Either cap the budget so the floor never reaches the part's underside (or the next lower surface) in that column, or refuse when the lowered part leaves no material under the cutter's footprint. Add a thin-plate pin (Engrave and Trace, aligned and turned) through generate and the post, plus a sim-credit unit pin in `crates/sim/tests/mark_credit.rs`.
2. NeoTech's item 2 (shank and holder judged against the lowered part) stands as written. I have nothing to add to it.

My other notes stand: the Milling-test Adaptive2D generator gouge, the cross-part gap, the cutter-scaled budget and the no-stock stand-down. All test and clippy results in my first review are unchanged.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 4f05e9c0f17f264e7ecfbea3267bf24ae9b66c2f -->
**Delta re-review of 976cda6c..4f05e9c0 (one commit, no merges): no blockers found.** For our part, this review clears head 4f05e9c0. **NeoTech's requested changes and the `needs-rework` label stay in place until NeoTech re-checks this head.** I have not added `merge-ready` and have not removed any label.

### What looks good
- **Through-cut (NeoTech item 1, our correction item 1).** Both judges now read the floor from the same geometry. On the operation side, `verify::seat_skin` raises every underside by `MARK_FLOOR` (0.2 mm) into closed prisms, and the edge is swept against them with the same solid law (`mark_law.rs:164-165`). On the sim side, the credit floor is `max(sweep, top - budget, highest underside + MARK_FLOOR)` (`stock_sim/mark.rs:77-93`). Both read the same `verify::undersides` and one constant. Both fail closed: an unreadable mesh gives the sim no credit, and a facet the op cannot read is kept as an underside. A column with no underside returns an infinite floor, which `credit_floors` skips (`edge_break.rs:87-89`), so it keeps its sharp verdict.
- **Undersides are found by ray parity, not by winding.** A face shared by two bodies is not treated as an underside (pinned in the `seat` unit tests, and confirmed end to end by the stacked-touching probe below). The roof of a void is treated as an underside.
- **Shank and holder (item 2).** From the lowered-part reading only the edge's `Gouge` is kept. The stack is judged by `verify::stack_hits` against the part as it actually stands, and rapids no longer get the budget. The excuse is narrow: `stack_only`, 3-axis, no arc, the same XY, Z not falling, and starting exactly where the previous cutting move ended (`solid.rs:191-195`). It is pinned on both sides: a rapid sideways, down, or from elsewhere is still convicted.
- The through-cut note names the floor. There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. `seat.rs` has a provenance line and lives in the crate that owns the solid law. `mark_floor.rs` is in `crates/app/tests` (it drives commands) and has a gate map. No new crate edge was added, and the decision file records the floor, the alternatives that were dropped, the conservative costs, the excuse, and #1621 for the cross-part gap.

### Results merged with `upstream/main` c00ba18a (built locally on macOS with sccache)
The self-hosted runner was not usable because the runner list returned 403, so everything ran locally. The trial merge was clean.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-sim lib + every sim test binary (incl. `mark_credit` 9, `edge_break_credit` 5) | all passed, 0 failed (lib 157) |
| app `mark_floor` (new) / `engrave_law` / `keep_law` / `whole_model_pocket` | 4 / 9 / 7 / 5 passed |
| app `lead_approach` / `trochoid_law` / `slot_picks` / `slot_pick_refusals` | 6 / 6 / 8 / 3 passed |
| app `circular_entity_law` / `circular_pick_law` / `solid_law` / `solid_law_goldens` / `golden_cl` | 4 / 4 / 4 / 7 / 33 passed |
| app `verify` / `mcp_verify` / `posting` / `operations` | 21 / 3 / 17 / 119 passed |
| app `machine_switch` / `post_not_judged` / `setup_stock_source` / `stock_source_verdict` / `edge_break_gate` | 6 / 4 / 8 / 22 / 5 passed |
| app lib | 252 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Adversarial probes.** These came from a throwaway test file that was not pushed. Each used a whole-model Engrave **and** Trace with EM-0600-4FL on aligned and turned stock. The sim column applies to aligned stock only.

| Part | Cut | Op | Aligned (sim) | Turned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40x40x2 plate (our repro) | Top 2, Bottom -0.9 | Gouge, "cuts through" | refused (sim worst 1.10) | refused |
| same | to Z0.1 (0.1 left) | Gouge | refused (sim 0.10) | refused |
| same | to Z0.2 (floor exactly) / Z1.7 | clean | posts (sim 0) | posts |
| 1.5 mm wide, 2 mm thick lip under the x=-20 edge (cutter half off the part, half lip, part 10 mm thick) | 1.9 deep / 1.5 deep | Gouge / clean | refused (0.10) / posts | refused / posts |
| Edge running from a 2 mm deck to 10 mm solid along the path | 1.9 / 1.5 | Gouge / clean | refused / posts | refused / posts |
| Internal closed void, roof 1.5 under the top | 1.4 / 1.2 | Gouge / clean | refused (0.10) / posts | refused / posts |
| Tilted underside (Z0 to Z1.5 under a flat top at 2) | to Z1.65 / Z1.85 | Gouge / clean | refused (sim 0.048, the expected 0.05 at cell centre) / posts | refused / posts |
| Two bodies, gap: 2 mm plate over a block | 1.9 / 1.5 | Gouge / clean | refused / posts | refused / posts |
| Two bodies, touching (1+1 mm) | to Z0.1 / to Z1.0 | Gouge / clean | refused / posts | refused / posts |

In every case the two judges agree, and partial overlap at the cutter's edge is caught.

**Mutation checks (my own, each reverted, tree confirmed restored):**

| Mutation | Red |
|---|---|
| `MARK_FLOOR` = 0 | `mark_floor` x3, `mark_credit` x2 |
| sim floor without the `underside + MARK_FLOOR` term | `mark_floor` sim verdict, `mark_credit` x3 |
| `seat_skin` skipped in `mark_into` | `mark_floor` x2, `mark_law` units x2 |
| excuse widened: any vertical lift (not only from a cut's end) | `only_the_retract_up_the_marks_own_kerf...` |
| excuse widened: any upward rapid after a cut (XY test dropped) | same unit |
| `stack_hits` against the lowered part | `mark_floor` shank-in-kerf, `mark_law` units x3 |

The author's M13-M19 table is consistent with these.

### Requested before merge
None from this review. NeoTech's own requested change stands until NeoTech re-checks.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **The kerf-retract excuse skips the whole assembly, not just the edge** (`solid.rs:193-195`, `continue`). Below the start pose this is sound, because the stack was judged there on the cutting move. But a holder lifting straight up into material *above* the modelled assembly (an overhang over the end of an open Trace chain) is now judged by nothing on that rapid. A tighter form would still judge the lift's shank and holder band against the unlowered part and excuse only the edge band. I could not build a realistic 3-axis mark that reaches this, so it is a note, not a blocker.
2. `undersides` runs four column reads per facet, and it runs in both the op law and the sim credit. That cost is fine on these fixtures. It is worth watching on large STEP meshes.
3. My earlier notes stand: the Milling-test Adaptive2D generator gouge, the cutter-scaled budget (now recorded for the maintainer as options a/b/c), the no-stock stand-down, and the cross-part gap (#1621). `generate.rs` is already over 400 lines and grew by a few lines. `solid.rs` grew from 177 to 211.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 4f05e9c0f17f264e7ecfbea3267bf24ae9b66c2f -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** One item is left: the new rapid-lift exemption skips the shank and holder entirely. Both items from the 976cda6c review are fixed and pinned in both judges.

This re-reviews the delta `976cda6c..4f05e9c0` (one commit, 11 files) and re-reads the whole mark law.

### Requested at 976cda6c: how each was settled

**1. Through-cut on a plate thinner than the budget: refused in both judges.**
- **Operation law** (`crates/app/src/operation/mark_law.rs:164`):
  - The edge is also swept with the solid law against `verify::seat_skin(facets, MARK_FLOOR)`. That is every underside raised into a closed prism 0.2 mm high.
  - An edge that enters it is a blocking `Warning::Gouge`, and the path gets the "cuts through the part" note.
  - Straight and XY-arc moves are swept exactly, so a 0.2 mm slab cannot fall between samples.
  - An unreadable mesh still fails closed. `undersides` builds the same `SolidIndex` as the lowered reading, which returns a `Gouge` at the first cut on failure.
- **Sim credit** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/mark.rs:79-92`):
  - The floor is `max(sweep, top - budget, highest underside + MARK_FLOOR)`.
  - An unreadable part, or a column with no underside, gets no credit: an infinite floor is skipped in `credit_floors`.
  - An emptied column has a non-finite sim top and is skipped too.
  - `posting_sim.rs:73` blocks on `gouge_cells > 0`.
- **Pins.** Read against the old code, each of these fails there:
  - `mark_floor.rs::a_cut_through_a_thin_plate_gouges_and_never_posts_on_either_stock`. The old law gave 0 gouges and no note, and it posted.
  - `mark_credit.rs::a_budget_deeper_than_the_plate_never_credits_a_cut_through_it`. The old floor `max(z, p - 2.9)` lay under the plate.
  - The 0.1 mm-web cases in both files.
  - `the_program_sim_never_credits_a_cut_through_the_plate`.
  - The void-roof units in `seat.rs` and `mark_credit.rs`.

**2. Shank and holder judged against the lowered part: fixed for cutting moves.**
- From the lowered reading only the edge's `Gouge` is kept (`mark_law.rs:160`).
- The stack goes through `verify::stack_hits` against the part as it stands (`mark_law.rs:167`).
- Pinned by `mark_floor.rs::a_shank_in_the_kerf_is_judged_against_the_part_as_it_stands`.

### Results merged with main
On the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43552150467. It ran on the macOS `camcraft-pr-test` runner, merged with main c00ba18a, and was green.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| quick gate: sim suites | ok, 122 s |
| quick gate: motion suites | ok, 4 s |
| quick gate: app suites | ok, 883 s |
| quick gate: ui suites | ok, 39 s |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Wall time 17.5 min, 4 steps, 0 failed. No local build or test runs were made for this review.

### Requested before merge
1. **The rapid-lift exemption skips the shank and holder entirely.**
   - **Where.** `crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs:191-195` `continue`s past every check for a straight rapid up the tool axis that starts where the previous cutting move ended.
   - **Why it is only partly justified.** The exemption is right for the edge, which rides its own kerf through part material the lowered law permits. It is not right for the shank and holder.
   - **What it misses.** At the end of the cutting move the stack was judged only where it stood, up to the holder's top (`reach`). The lift then sweeps the holder up to clearance through space nothing judged.
   - **The case.** An overhang of the part above the end point of an open engraving line, above the holder's top and below clearance. The holder lifts into it, and the program posts clean.
   - **What it loosened.** At 976cda6c that lift was still judged against the lowered part, and an overhang thicker than the budget was convicted. Now nothing judges it.
   - **Nothing else catches it.** Mark kinds carry their own solid law in `generate.rs`. I could not show that any other judge covers this move, and no test pins it.
   - **Fix.** On the exempted lift, still judge the non-edge atoms (`body`: shank and holder) against the part as it stands, and skip only the edge. At the end of a mark the shank stands above the finished surface (the edge is within its flute), so this reading stays clean for a normal retract and convicts only real steel-on-part.
   - **Pin.** An overhang above the end of an open Engrave/Trace line, refused on both stocks, plus the plain retract still posting.

### What looks good
- One constant, `MARK_FLOOR`, read by both judges.
- Undersides are read by vertical-ray parity, never by winding. This is pinned with flipped facets and with a face lying between two bodies.
- `Marked` counts each reading separately. A cut within the budget that breaks through gets only the floor note, and that is pinned.
- The decision file records the 0.2 mm floor and the alternatives that were dropped.
- `verify/seat.rs` has a provenance line.
- The body carries `Fixes #1595`, `Fixes #1603` and an updated `Changelog:`.
- No golden, snapshot or `PROCESS_VERSION` change.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **A through-cut's depth is understated.** The sim charges a through-cut from the floor, so a 2 mm plate cut right through reports a worst gouge of about 0.2 mm (pinned that way in `mark_credit.rs`). It still blocks, because blocking is on `gouge_cells`, but the depth in the refusal text understates the damage.
2. **Not exercised:**
   - No local build was made; the build and tests are the runner's.
   - No test covers a through-cut on a tilted 3+2 plane. That arm passes local facets, so the skin is read along the tool, but only stock turned about Z is pinned.
   - The two earlier non-blocking notes (the `budget_of` empty-facets half, and 3+2 budget agreement) are still open.
3. `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` was already far over 400 lines (3529) and grows by a few. Not blocking.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
